subject: Availability accounting procedure & credit matrix — Hyperion RFP follow-up
messages:
From: Jessica Hart <jessica.hart@hyperionfs.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alan White <alan.white@hyperionfs.com>, procurement@hyperionfs.com
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Clarification on availability measurement for RFP (Section 6.2/6.3)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the RFP response — the team reviewed your SLA section and we have a few clarifying questions before we finalize scoring:

1) Measurement window and sampling: Do you measure availability on a calendar-month basis or on a rolling 30-day window? What is your sampling cadence for synthetic checks or production request sampling?

2) Failure definition: Does Redwood count a latency breach (exceeding configured p95) as a failure for availability, or only outright errors (5xx)?

3) Exclusions: Please confirm which events are excluded from measurement (scheduled maintenance windows, force-majeure, customer-caused faults). Do you require notice periods for planned maintenance to be excluded?

4) Service credits: We need the full credit calculation and cap for recurring SLA violations (percentage of monthly invoice, remedy steps).

5) Dispute window & evidence: What logs/exports will you provide if we dispute a measurement and what is the turnaround?

Could you provide a short worked example (numbers) and any attachments (measurement script or appendix) that your team uses? We aim to close the SLA scoring by next week.

Best,
Jessica
Jessica Hart
Sr. Procurement Manager, Hyperion Financial Systems

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jessica Hart <jessica.hart@hyperionfs.com>
Cc: Alan White <alan.white@hyperionfs.com>

Subject: RE: Clarification on availability measurement for RFP (Section 6.2/6.3)

Hi Jessica — thanks for the clear list. Below is our standard availability accounting approach and the service-credit matrix we propose for the contract. I attached our "Redwood Availability Appendix v1" (PDF) and a small example measurement script as a reference.

Summary (short):
- Measurement window: Calendar month (UTC) by default; rolling 30-day window available by request as a contract option.
- Sampling: Synthetic checks + production sampling. Synthetic probes run from three regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) every 30s; production sampling aggregates success/latency from request logs at 1s resolution.
- Failure definition: Availability is primarily based on successful responses (2xx) for the model endpoint. Latency SLOs (p95) are measured separately and can trigger service credits if breached per the latency credit schedule below.
- Exclusions: Scheduled maintenance (>=72 hours notice for planned infra work), force majeure, customer-caused misconfiguration, and third-party cloud provider outages are excluded. Emergency maintenance with shorter notice is excluded when declared by Redwood.

Detailed measurement methodology:
- Measurement unit: A sample is any attempted inference request (synthetic or production) that receives a definitive outcome within 60s.
- Availability calculation (per calendar month):
  Availability % = (Total successful samples - Excluded samples) / (Total attempted samples - Excluded samples) * 100
  "Successful" = HTTP 2xx AND runtime model returned result within 60s.
- Latency SLOs: p50/p95/p99 are computed over the set of successful samples using request-response latency from the serving logs. Cold-starts are marked and excluded from p95 calculation if they are caused by model loading for capacity scaling (documented in logs).
- Multi-region sampling: We compute both a global aggregate and per-region aggregates. Global availability is the weighted average by volume; per-region outages are reported separately.

Service credit matrix (monthly):
- Availability >= 99.95%: no credit.
- Availability >= 99.5% and < 99.95%: 5% of monthly service fees for the affected service(s).
- Availability >= 99.0% and < 99.5%: 10% of monthly service fees for the affected service(s).
- Availability < 99.0%: 25% of monthly service fees for the affected service(s), up to a 100% cap over consecutive months (see contract).

Latency credits (applies independently of availability):
- p95 latency target (example): 450ms for baseline large-generic model under agreed request profile.
- p95 breach > 450ms and <= 750ms: 3% credit.
- p95 breach > 750ms and <= 1500ms: 7% credit.
- p95 breach > 1500ms: 15% credit.

Worked example (calendar month):
- Total attempted samples: 2,700,000 (1M synthetic + 1.7M prod aggregated).
- Excluded (maintenance & provider outage): 30,000.
- Successful samples: 2,655,000.
- Availability = (2,655,000) / (2,700,000 - 30,000) = 2,655,000 / 2,670,000 = 99.44% => triggers 10% credit on affected services.

Dispute process & evidence:
- You may raise a dispute within 30 days after the monthly report is published.
- Redwood will provide: sampling logs (time, region, request id, code, latency), synthetic probe history, and the measurement script output used for the month.
- Turnaround: initial acknowledgement within 2 business days, full analysis within 10 business days.

Additional notes:
- Fallbacks/overrides: If we failover to a lower-capacity cluster or compatible model variant for capacity constraints, we treat requests served by the fallback as successful for availability if the response meets success criteria. If a fallback materially reduces capability (e.g., truncated responses or missing plugins), we flag the period and discuss remediation credits case-by-case.
- Caps and stacking: Credits for availability and latency may both apply but are capped at 100% of monthly fees for the affected service.

Attachments: redwood_availability_appendix_v1.pdf (detailed definitions and example queries), measurement_script_example.sh (synthetic probe script).

If useful, I can include a short numeric spreadsheet with per-day samples and the exact monthly calculation for your team to inspect.

Best regards,

Hi Jessica — looping in Laura from our legal team to confirm exclusion/fallback wording. Laura — any edits to the appendix before I send the "final for RFP" copy?

Jessica, one quick clarification you asked in your initial note (latency vs availability): our availability calculation focuses on correctness/errors/timeouts. Latency is measured as an independent SLO with its own credit schedule. We've kept the two separate so you can choose to include latency credits in the contract if you want both protections.

Kim

Subject: RE: Availability accounting procedure & credit matrix — Hyperion RFP follow-up

Thanks — that's largely helpful. Two quick follow-ups before we close:

1) For latency SLO measurement, do you report p95 per model variant (e.g., rwd-large v1.2) or only per endpoint alias? We need to ensure measurements align with our test profile (burst vs steady).

2) For maintenance exclusions, 72-hour notice is fine for planned infra work; can you commit to at least one emergency maintenance notification channel (email + status.redwoodinference.com post) and note when the exclusion takes effect?

If you can confirm those two bullets in a final email (and the updated appendix with legal edits), we'll mark the SLA section as accepted on our side.

Best,
Jessica

Subject: RE: Availability accounting procedure & credit matrix — Hyperion RFP follow-up

Jessica — final clarifications:

1) Latency measurement granularity: We compute p50/p95/p99 at both the endpoint alias level and per-model-variant. For contract purposes we can specify that the canonical reported metric is the endpoint alias p95 (aggregated by variant by traffic-weight). We will also provide per-variant breakdowns in monthly reports so you can map to your test profiles (burst vs steady).

2) Emergency maintenance notification: We will publish emergency maintenance notices to both status.redwoodinference.com and send an email to the customer's primary SLA contact within 2 hours of declaration. The exclusion takes effect at the declared start time in the notice.

Next steps: Laura will provide contract-safe language on the fallback/exclusion paragraphs; I will attach the updated appendix and send a stamped copy for your RFP binder by COB Monday.

Thanks again — appreciate the quick turnaround from your end.
